turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hey there, how have things been?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My nephew is starting engineering and his parents want my advice on a laptop.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm going to describe each one. Save your comments until the end.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A powerful workstation laptop with a strong graphics card, which handles design software but costs nearly two thousand.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A mid range laptop with good memory, decent graphics, about nine hundred, and a little heavy.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A cheap thin laptop for notes and emails, with him using the university's computer labs for heavy work.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: I'd go with the mid range laptop, it handles most first year software and costs half the workstation. Check the course's recommended specs before buying, though. The cheap option only works if the labs are really accessible.
